_comment: Request flows for the step-through player. Each step names the diagram nodes and edges it lights up, and the file (and function, checked to exist in that file) where it happens.

flows.title: Opening a page
flows.summary: A page address becomes a file by way of site/site.json. Nothing else on disk can be reached.

steps.title: The browser asks for an address
steps.text: Typing /materials, following a link, or an old address such as /market_place_1.html.

steps.title: The guards run first
steps.text: The Host header must be this machine (or in ALLOWED_HOSTS), otherwise the answer is 421 before anything else happens. Every response then gets nosniff and no-referrer.

steps.title: site.json turns the address into a page
steps.text: The route table is built once from site/site.json: page routes, aliases (301 to the canonical route), design-time names (302). An address that is not in it is a 404; the file system is never searched.

steps.title: The built page is sent
steps.text: pages/<page>.html with Cache-Control: no-cache and conditional-request support, plus the page's own headers from site.json.

steps.title: Photos and videos come from /media
steps.text: The page asks for /media/m02-terracotta.jpg. Only allowed extensions are served, dot-segments and traversal are refused, and Range requests work so video seeks.

flows.title: Rebuilding the pages from a new Claude Design export
flows.summary: pages_original/ plus JSON patches become pages/. A changed export fails loudly instead of being half-patched.

steps.title: Drop the new export in place
steps.text: Replace the file in pages_original/ under the same name (index.html, market_place.html, dashboard.html). These are never edited and never served.

steps.title: site.json says what is what
steps.text: Each page lists its source export and its built file; linkStyle decides whether links in the pages point at routes (/materials) or file names.

steps.title: npm run build:site
steps.text: The build reads site.json, decodes each export's bundle (template plus compressed assets) and applies the page's patch file.

steps.title: Anchored JSON patches
steps.text: site/patches/<page>.json is a list of steps: relink design-time names and insert the navigation entries from components.json. Every anchor must match exactly the expected number of times, otherwise the build stops and says which step.

steps.title: pages/ is written
steps.text: The built pages are written and committed. An untouched bundle round-trips byte for byte, so only the patched parts differ from the export.

steps.title: The links are checked
steps.text: npm run check:links verifies that every same-site link resolves, that every page links to the pages site.json requires, and that no design-time name is left. npm run check:site rebuilds in memory and only reports.

flows.title: Starting up
flows.summary: npm start builds the pages if they are missing, then Express reads its settings, assembles the app and listens.

steps.title: npm start
steps.text: The prestart hook builds the pages if they are missing, then node app.js runs. Settings come from .env (or TERUCON_ENV_FILE) with the real environment winning.

steps.title: The settings are read
steps.text: HOST, PORT and ALLOWED_HOSTS come from the env file and the real environment, which wins. The file is re-read whenever it changes; HOST and PORT are used when the server starts listening.

steps.title: site.json is loaded
steps.text: site/site.json is read and checked once. A route that is not a path, or a file outside the project, stops the start with a message that says where.

steps.title: The app is assembled
steps.text: The security headers and the guards come first, then the pages, the overview, the media and the API. An unknown address under /api/ is a JSON 404, anything else a plain 404, and the error handler comes last.

steps.title: The server listens
steps.text: It listens on HOST and PORT and prints the addresses of the site and of this overview, and which settings file it read. A busy port ends with a message and exit code 1.

steps.title: Ctrl+C stops it cleanly
steps.text: SIGINT and SIGTERM close the server: idle connections end at once, busy ones get two seconds, then the process exits with 0.
